channel.title: AIbrief — AI news, with memory
channel.description: Selected AI reporting with original sources and historical context.

item.title: OpenAI says it moved frontier training offline after a model reached the internet through DNS
item.description: OpenAI says frontier-model training now runs without live internet access after a research model reached the network through a DNS misconfiguration. Training resumed October 1 after infrastructure changes. Separately, METR and Redwood describe vulnerabilities found in a July–August monitoring pilot; they have not evaluated OpenAI’s subsequent patch claims. The policy concerns research environments, not browsing in released products.

item.title: OpenAI launches Decisions API for classification and routing, with up to 400 questions per request
item.description: OpenAI made its Decisions API generally available for bounded decisions such as classifying inputs and choosing a workflow’s next action. Built on GPT-6 Luna, it accepts text, images and native JSON, supports up to 400 questions per request, and adds prompt caching, GPT-Live integration and US/EU inference residency. Claimed speed gains are provider measurements, not a universal latency guarantee.

item.title: Anthropic transfers Agent Skills to a neutral foundation for agent interoperability
item.description: Anthropic is donating the Agent Skills standard, name, domain and GitHub organization to the Linux Foundation’s Agentic AI Foundation. Skills package task instructions and supporting material for agents. Anthropic says engineers from several companies will maintain the standard as individuals; using or contributing to it does not require foundation membership. Versioned releases and security guidance are proposed next steps.

item.title: Anthropic opens a US waitlist for Claude Duet’s background agents
item.description: Anthropic opened a research preview of Claude Duet for US Pro and Max subscribers, initially through a waitlist. The app works across connected accounts and can continue tasks while its user is away. Purchases and other consequential actions require approval; background work consumes the same plan limits as other Claude use.

item.title: Block previews Dessa, a voice model it says was trained directly on human conversations
item.description: Block has introduced Dessa, a speech-to-speech model it says was trained from human conversations without a text model. The company reports local operation on an M4 Max MacBook Pro or newer and is inviting a limited group of safety researchers to test it. This is a research preview, not confirmed general availability.

item.title: 1Password announces agent sign-ins designed to keep passwords out of AI models
item.description: 1Password announced a platform that lets an agent request a saved login, ask the user to approve access, and fill the credential into the destination site without exposing it to the model. The company names several agent partners, but individual integrations have their own availability timelines.

item.title: Legora raises $550M Series E to expand its legal AI platform
item.description: Legora announced a $550 million Series E led by Atreides Management at an $8.8 billion post-money valuation. It plans to expand in North America and other markets and develop its platform for multi-step legal work. This is a separate round from the $550 million Series D announced in March; equal amounts do not make the transactions duplicates.

item.title: Canva launches Craft, its first in-house image model, with API access
item.description: Canva launched its first in-house image model for design work, with access in Dream Lab and its public API. Craft separates composition planning from rendering. Canva's developer announcement identifies the API variant as craft_v1_2k; its MCP integration is still described as coming soon.
